script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 12. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Every night, you experience vivid hallucinations that feel completely real—then forget almost all of them.  Dreams seem meaningless, but they might serve crucial functions: processing emotions, consolidating memories, even rehearsing threats.  Why does your brain create these nightly movies?

Dreams often feature emotionally significant content. REM sleep may help process and regulate emotions—people deprived of dream sleep become more emotionally reactive. Dreams might be therapy you give yourself every night. Many discoveries came in dreams: the structure of benzene, the sewing machine, songs and stories.  While you sleep, your brain makes connections your waking mind misses.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: The mind works on problems even when you're not aware.  Dreams teach that trusting the process means trusting work you can't see.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Dream Journal - Capture the Unconscious.

Here's your activity: Keep paper by your bed. When you wake, immediately write whatever you remember—even fragments. After a week, look for patterns: recurring themes, emotions, situations. Your dreaming mind might be telling you something your waking mind doesn't want to hear. This helps you notice patterns in dreams.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why we dream can be applied to dream journal - capture the unconscious. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
